links.reason: 694 answers the claim நோயில்லை வாழி கடவுள் (the god has no disease), while 673 praises a Lord who is திரையான் நரையான், without wrinkle or grey hair, and who does not eat: related portraits, but 694 is not an answer to 673's words. The teaches sentence is only the general point that the debate attacks the founder's body, and whether கடவுள் is the founder is itself uncertain.
links.text_issue: both verses flagged uncertain by the marker

links.reason: The quatrain's five gates (மெய்வாய்கண் மூக்குச் செவி) and the chain's வாயில் ஆறும், with ஊறு, நுகர்வு and வேட்கை following, are accurately set side by side. But the unit lists உள்ளமும் வாயிலும் as meeting objects rather than naming the mind a gate, and nothing in it says where the chain is cut, so the closing claim of teaches goes beyond the Tamil.

259 has the monk say சித்தமே அல்லதில்லை and that what is called தீங்கொழுக்கு is not தீவினை; 261 answers that only when உள்ளமும் பாயிரமும் ஒக்கும் is there release, refusing to split intent from act. The later verse answers the earlier directly and the conflict is the debate's own; the reading of பாயிரம் as outward conduct is needed but fits the reply.
links.text_issue: பாயிரம் read as outward conduct (bāhya) is uncertain

links.reason: The fire god's பண்டேயோர் ஏவலுடையேன் (21.51-52) and Kannaki's சீறினேன் குற்றமிலேன் (21.42) are rightly paired. But the patikam lines tie the former-birth curse (இட்ட சாபம் கட்டியது) to the couple's ripe deed and the husband seen only in divine form, not to the burning of the city, so the teaches sentence's three causes of the burning misattributes the curse.

Kar Narpathu 1 makes the rainbow the garland on the chest of பொருகடல் வண்ணன், and Mullaippattu 1-6 makes the rising cloud like நீர்செல நிமிர்ந்த மாஅல்; both open the mullai rains with Mal. The shift from the god's growing body to his adorned chest is a true and specific difference in how the same figure is used.

The unit defines அன்னுவயம் with the stock example சத்தம் அநித்தம் கிருத்தம் ஆதலின் (sound is impermanent because made), a lesson in the form of inference. Kural 331 condemns நில்லாதவற்றை நிலையின என்றுணரும் புல்லறிவு, a moral error about worldly things; the shared word for impermanence is all that joins them, and the Kural gains no 'form of proof' from a rule about sound.

The two rites do share items: a red-flower garland bound with fibre (மரல்வகுந்து தொடுத்த செம்பூங் கண்ணி / ஆர்நார் உரிவையின் செம்பூங் கரந்தை) and the names on the stone (பெயர்பொறித்து / பல்பெயர் மண்ணி). But 'almost item by item' overstates (no cairn or peacock feather in 269), and in 269 the stones are on a road already crossed, cited by the friend to comfort the wife (வந்தனர் விரைந்தே), not to fill her fear.

14.49-54 has Indra send rain so that Aputhiran's bowl finds no beggars (இரப்போர்க் காணாது ஏமாந்திருப்ப); 24.171-172 has the ascetic say that since Punniyarajan's birth பெயல் பிழைப்பு அறியாது, in the city of இந்திரன் மருமான். The later unit reverses the earlier: the plenty that idled his charity is now the mark of his merit, which the note and teaches state.

பான்மையில் திரியாது describes the crescent's light in a scene of Madhavi and Kovalan; the moon is called the Pandya line's founder (தென்னர் குலமுதல்) but no claim is made about the line's rule. The king's யானே கள்வன் in kaathai 20 does not contradict a description of the moon, so the tension rests entirely on reading the moon's constancy as a thesis about Pandya justice.

214 argues that flesh or an eye given cannot join another body (பரகாயம் ஒன்றாகுமே...காகமே உண்ணும்), so the gift helps no one; 360 argues that giving the body to a beast kills the many lives within it (உடம்பினுள்ள பல்லுயிர் சாவ), likening it to poisoning common water. Two distinct objections to the same birth-story gifts from two debates, accurately described.

The unit closes the fallacy lesson with ஐயம் இன்றி அறிந்து கொள் ஆய்ந்து, knowing true from false in inferences; Kural 357's ஓர்த்து...ஒருதலையா is about knowing உள்ளது so that birth need not be thought of. The epic does not tie this method to release, and the word ஏகாந்தம் that teaches makes the hinge does not occur in the unit.

The brahmin's maxim பத்தினி இல்லோர் பல அறம் செய்யினும் புத்தேள் உலகம் புகாஅர் is a genuine converse of Kural 58's பெற்றாற் பெறின் பெறுவர் பெண்டிர்...புத்தேளிர் வாழும் உலகு. But the age of sixty and Visakai's denial are not in this unit, so the link leans on the next scene, and the epic side's gain is only the couplet restated.

The king lists three possible causes, செங்கோல் கோடியோ செய் தவம் பிழைத்தோ...கற்புக் குறைபட்டோ, and says அறியேன; the deity names none and promises the maiden's bowl and Indra's rain. Against Kural 559's முறைகோடி மன்னவன் செயின்...ஒல்லாது வானம் பெயல, this is a case where the rule is received but cannot be applied, as the note says.

205's catalogue (கண்கொடுத்தான்...உடம்பினையும் பிளந்திட்டுப் பிறர்க்கீந்தான்) does make literal the couplet's என்பும் உரியர் பிறர்க்கு. But the gift of wife and child (பெண்கொடுத்தான், மகக்கொடுத்தான்) is not a gift of one's body, Neelakesi's 'madness' reply is outside the unit, and the epic-side gain is vague.

Kural 550 is about putting killers to death (கொலையிற் கொடியாரை வேந்தொறுத்தல்), while the unit has the king turn the prison into a house for the virtuous (சிறையோர் கோட்டம் அறவோர்க்கு ஆக்கினன்). The pairing is real but loose: the unit says nothing on whether the cruel must still be punished, so the teaches claim that the king does not deny it is unsupported.

58 is the plan to break the sage's மனநிறை and make him drop his vow; 72 has every wile meet இவையெனை எமக்கு. This is a plan and its defeat, a fulfilment reversed, not two incompatible claims, so tension is the wrong type, though the reading of where the vow's safety lies is fair.

The patikam's அரைசியல் பிழைத்தோர்க்கு அறம்கூற்று ஆவதூஉம் is applied by the bhutas' கோமுறை பிழைத்த நாளில் இந்நகர் தீமுறை உண்பதோர் திறனுண்டு, which extends the penalty to the city and calls it a rule the guardians know as their duty (தாமுறையாக அறிந்தனம்). The link rests on 103-106, not on the doubted portrait lines.
links.text_issue: lines 89-96 of the unit are doubted in the edition; the link does not rest on them

links.reason: 177 has Kundalakesi report that her teacher முந்துரைத்தான் முந்நூலும் and then the five aggregates; 477 shows the Buddha naming சூத்திரம், வினையம், சாத்திரம். The note's 'and then the aggregates' is not in 477, and the link is largely the debate's structure, report then source, which the plot already gives.

652's இருசார் வினைப்பயனும் செய்தார்கள் தாம் and Kural 319's தமக்கு இன்னா...தாமே வரும் agree that the doer reaps. Teaches reads the couplet's முற்பகல்/பிற்பகல் as limiting it to one day of one life, but that timing is rhetorical; the real point, whether a self persists across births to reap, is the debate's and not a qualification of the couplet.

155's தாம் செய் தீவினைக் கடல் and போதரும் புணை படைத்தாய் set beside Kural 10's பிறவிப் பெருங்கடல் நீந்துவர்...இறைவன் அடிசேராதார் show the same sea with two accounts of crossing: the sea is made of the swimmers' own deeds and the Jina makes a raft, while the couplet names only reaching the Lord's feet. The qualification is real and the gains are both true.

In 9.55-56 Devanthi explains the trouble by a vow broken in a former birth (பழம்பிறப்பில் பொய்த்தாய்) and prescribes the tanks; in 29.53-54 she says தீக்கனாக் கேட்டநாள் எய்த உணராதிருந்தேன், confessing she did not see what the dream would bring. The later unit reverses the earlier, as the note says.

5.218-223 has Death, fearing the king's sceptre (மன்னவன் செங்கோல் மறுத்தல் அஞ்சி), change from manly form to a woman's while keeping its deadly work (அருந்தொழில் திரியாது), and Kural 1083 finds Death in a woman's form (பெண்டகையால் பேரமர்க் கட்டு). The epic adds a cause, the just sceptre, to the couplet's lover's discovery, which is what the type claims.

574 has the Buddha say வினையும் உளது பயனும் உளது...செய்ஞ்ஞனம் இல்லை, with no aggregate lasting a moment; 614 answers that if the fruit comes வழிவழி later, then செய்கை சென்றுசென்று உண்டே, the deed persists. The Jain reply does show that a theory with deed and fruit but no lasting doer must place persistence somewhere.

The kuravai ends asking the Pandya's drum to bring victory (கடிப்பிகு முரசே) and the next lines have Madari return on hearing ஓர் ஊரரவம், the irony being real. But 18.1-15 does not report the guards' killing, as the note says it does: Madari comes back and stands silent (சொல்லாடாள்), and the two units are consecutive, so the link adds little to the plot order.

Madhavi lists three kinds of pathini, each introduced by ஆயின் as a fallback, and sets Kannaki above all three (அத் திறத்தாளும் அல்லள்), so she does not praise dying with the husband as the highest chastity. The cemetery's ஒருங்குடன் மாய்ந்த பெண்டிர்க்கு shrines are a real echo, but teaches misstates Madhavi's ranking.

2.73-75 has மாசறு பொன்னே...அரும்பெறல் பாவாய் among endearments for her beauty, and 16.86-90 has பொன்னே கொடியே...நாணின் பாவாய் for one who came with நாணமும் மடனும்...கற்பும் பெருந்துணையாக. The same words return with a new ground, her chastity and following, which is what teaches claims.

Kovalan's plan (சிலம்பு முதலாக...உலந்தபொருள் ஈட்டுதல் உற்றேன்) is in the same breath credited to the deed (வினைகடைக் கூட்ட வியம்கொண்டான்), and Kural 380 says fate comes first even when one devises another way (மற்றொன்று சூழினுந் தான்முந் துறும்). The epic adds that the counter-plan itself is fate's road, a specific addition.

Both couplets do use fire of the belly (தீயளவு; பசியென்னும் தீப்பிணி). But the teaches sentence, that the pair 'widens what not falling ill means', is a vague restatement of the shared theme rather than something the pair teaches.

Kannaki's பீடு அன்று refuses the tanks and Kama's shrine, and Kural 55's தெய்வம் தொழாஅள் கொழுநன் தொழுதெழுவாள் makes a natural gloss. But the unit gives no reason beyond பீடு அன்று, so reading the refusal as the couplet's wife needs a generous reading, and the epic-side gain presents that gloss as the rule that explains her.

7.289 has the narrator say ஊழ்வினை வந்து உருத்தது while Kovalan in 7.288 judges Madhavi மாயப்பொய் பலகூட்டும் மாயத்தாள்; in 9.69 he blames சலதி and 9.78 the narrator again names the deed. The two causes are layered, karma working through his judgment, rather than incompatible, and Kovalan's blame of Madhavi is already in 7 itself.

The kuravai's சேவகன்சீர் கேளாத செவி என்ன செவியே defines an organ by its worship, the same logic as Kural 9's கோளில் பொறியின் குணமிலவே...தாளை வணங்காத் தலை. Teaches is specific: the couplet's single head and unnamed god become a refrain run through each organ for a named god.

Aputhiran calls heaven a land where deeds done here are only enjoyed (ஈண்டுச் செய் வினை ஆண்டு நுகர்ந்திருத்தல்), with no one who does dharma or gives, and asks what its king could give one whose bowl ends hunger. Kural 222's மேலுலகம் இல்லெனினும் ஈதலே நன்று is pushed further: heaven is not only unneeded for giving but has no place for it.

The hymn makes blood the price of victory (மிடறுகு குருதிகொள் விறல்தரு விலையே) and Kural 259 sets not killing and eating above a thousand oblations. The note does say the conflict depends on the blood being a slain creature's, but whose throat bleeds is not stated, and the couplet's உயிர்செகுத்து உண்ணாமை concerns killing to eat, so the clash is real only on a narrow reading.
links.text_issue: marker flags the stanza's sense as uncertain

links.reason: The seers say Kovalan, reborn among the gods (தேவரில் தோற்றி), must still eat his evil deed (அத் தீவினை இன்னும் துய்த்து) and will reach release by hearing the Lord's dharma (நாதன் நல்லறம் கேட்டு வீடு எய்தும்); Tirumanthiram 2313 has the soul turned through சுவர்க்க நரகம் புவி and freed அருளால். Release after the deed is spent through teaching heard, against release by grace, is an incompatible claim of the kind the brief names.
links.text_issue: Tirumanthiram 2313's அறங்காண் and கிரங்கா are unclear

links.reason: Sudhamathi's ஊழ் தரு தவத்தள் சாப சரத்தி does invoke the power of tapas that Kural 264 names (ஒன்னார்த் தெறலும்...தவத்தான் வரும்). But the prince's shrug at line 21 and the failure to deter are outside the unit, so teaches and the other-side gain rest on a scene not shown.

Kural 329 calls those whose work is killing புலைவினையர், and the vari says கடல்புக்கு உயிர்க்கொன்று வாழ்வர்நின் ஐயர் without any judgment, turning it into a compliment. The pair is real and teaches is specific, but the song states no rule that limits the couplet: it is an unremarked conflict, closer to tension than qualification.

The deity names and rejects a defence, தலைவன் காக்கும் தம் பொருட்டு ஆகிய அவல வெவ் வினை, and says அறம் செய் காதல் அன்பினின் ஆயினும் மறம் செய்துளது எனின் வல் வினை ஒழியாது. Kural 319 says harm returns of itself but not whether a good motive changes that; the epic answers it does not, a true qualification.

காலம்அறி யாதோன் கையுறல் பொய் and Kural 484's ஞாலம் கருதினுங் கைகூடுங் காலம் கருதி share the image of gain coming to hand by timing. But the couplet makes time and place together (காலம் கருதி இடத்தாற் செயின்) the condition, so teaches' claim that it makes knowing the time alone enough misstates it.

Thuvathikan's prophecy that she will bear வறன் ஓடு உலகில் மழைவளம் தரூஉம் அறன் ஓடு (21.157-158) is fulfilled when the bowl feeds all who gather in Kanchi and plenty swells (28.227-233). A prophecy and its event, with the feeding put before the rain as the prophecy itself does.
links.text_issue: வசித் தொழில் (28.233) is a rare word whose reading as rain's work is not certain

links.reason: 29.37-39 calls Kannaki the one born on the வடபேரிமய மலை and bathed in the Ganga, the history of the stone, and 29.101 calls the image மலையரையன் பெற்ற மடப்பாவை set on kings' crowns. The second phrase also fits the mountain king's daughter, so the pair does show the woman being spoken of in a goddess's terms.

Madhavi's காதலன் உற்ற கடுந் துயர் கேட்டு போதல்செய்யா உயிரொடு நின்றே...நாணுத் துறந்தேன் is exactly the case Kural 1017 rules out: உயிர்ப்பொருட்டால் நாண்துறவார். She names herself as one who kept life at the cost of shame, and her tapas becomes her answer, which the couplet's two choices do not provide.

The cattle's bells fall (மான்மணி வீழும்) and the cows tremble (நடுங்குபு) in the herders' house, and the queen sees the umbrella and sceptre fall and the gate bell tremble (கோல்வீழ நின்று நடுங்கும் கடைமணி). The same signs, falling and a trembling bell, move from the hosts' cowshed to the king's gate as the wrong nears him.

The questions துறக்க வேந்தன் துய்ப்பிலன்கொல்லோ? அறக் கோல் வேந்தன் அருளிலன்கொல்லோ may clear the king or may genuinely ask whether he lacks grace, and the note admits the link holds only on the first reading. The epic-side gain, that the questions answer the Kural's doctrine, reads a reply to Kural 545 into lines that do not cite it, and துய்ப்பிலன் is itself uncertain.
links.text_issue: the sense of துய்ப்பிலன் (46) is uncertain
